ok r4 benign b1
text: Retrieval latency matters more than recall once agents run in production. We saw p95 drop from 900 ms to 240 ms when we cached embeddings per tenant.

name: ok r4 benign b2
text:
Agreed on the eval point. Most teams I talk to measure accuracy on a fixed set and never re-sample after launch.

The drift shows up in week three, not week one.

name: ok r4 benign b3
text: This matches what we see: the hard part is not the model, it's the handoff between steps. A 2% error per step compounds fast over 10 steps.

name: ok r4 benign b4
text: Strong take. I'd add one thing: cost per resolved ticket is a better north star than cost per token.

name: ok r4 benign b5
text:
We moved from 3 vendors to 1 in Q3 and the integration work dropped by roughly half.

Curious whether you saw the same after the switch?

name: ok r4 benign b6
text: The 2024–2025 budget cycle is when most of these pilots either scale or die.

name: ok r4 benign b7
text: e.g. a team of 5 can ship this in 2 weeks if the data is clean; i.e. most of the work is upstream.

name: ok r4 benign b8
text: Fair point… though I think the bottleneck moves to review, not generation.

name: ok r4 benign b9
text:
• Faster onboarding
• Fewer handoffs
• Clearer ownership
That third one is the one people skip.

name: ok r4 benign b10
text: We hit $1.2M ARR with 14 people, so I'm wary of the 'hire ahead of revenue' advice here.

name: ok r4 benign b11
text:
Version 2.0
was the turning point for us, mostly because of the new scheduler.

name: ok r4 benign b12
text: Café owners and naïve pricing models have more in common than you'd think — both underestimate the tail.

name: ok r4 benign b13
text: Our latency went from 1–2 s to under 300 ms after we moved the index closer to the workers.

name: ok r4 benign b14
text: Between 9 and 5, mostly. After hours it is a different story.
